No technique defeats a Gold Saint a second time. The first strike teaches you; the second finds you ready. Your cosmo reads an attack's structure the instant it lands and rebuilds you against it.

The first time each day a given creature deals damage to you with a specific attack, spell, or effect, note it. Every subsequent time that same effect from any source targets you, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC and saving throw against it, and resistance equal to your level to its damage.

You track adaptations for up to five distinct effects at once; if a sixth would be added, the oldest is forgotten. An 'effect' is a specific attack routine, not a damage type — a particular monster's claw Strike, a specific spell, a named technique. The GM adjudicates what counts as the same attack; reskinned or fundamentally altered versions do not.

Adapting mid-strike. Once per round, when you would be damaged by an effect you have already adapted to, you may use a reaction to heighten your adaptation: until the start of your next turn, your resistance to that effect increases to twice your level, and if the effect required a save, you improve your degree of success by one step.

Special On any day your Cloth's constellation is ascendant or Exalted, your cosmo reads faster than experience: you adapt to an effect the first time it damages you, rather than needing to have suffered it once before.
